hints.title: Why is a plain delimiter unsafe?
hints.body: If you join words with a character, a word may contain that character, so the decoder cannot tell a separator from data. You need a way to know where each word ends.

hints.title: Put the length first
hints.body: Write the word's length in decimal, then `'#'`, then the word. The decoder reads digits until `'#'`, converts them to a number, and then consumes exactly that many characters. This works even when the word itself contains `'#'`.

hints.title: Handle both directions and the empty cases
hints.body: Encoding no words produces the empty string. Encoding one empty word produces `"0#"`. Decoding the empty string produces no words. For each operation, append the appropriate list to the result; an encode result is a one-element list containing the encoded text.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
encode(words):
    result = ""
    for word in words:
        result += decimal(length(word)) + "#" + word
    return result

decode(text):
    words = []
    index = 0
    while index < length(text):
        marker = position of '#' at or after index
        size = integer from text[index:marker]
        start = marker + 1
        words.append(text[start:start + size])
        index = start + size
    return words
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
